parsing_res_list.block_content: THURSDAY, JUNE 4, 1925.
THE CHINA MAIL.

Yesterday the King's Birthday was honoured in Hongkong with the usual loyalty, the principal toast and expression at Club and many homes being the health and prosperity of His Majesty and the hope that he might long be spared to reign over his subjects.

According to Reuter, congratulations on the King's sixtieth birthday began to arrive at the Palace early in the morning, including messages from all over the Empire. The Prince of Wales and Prince George, the latter on route to Weihaiwei from Shanghai, cabled their congratulations also. The official celebration was the trooping of the colours of the Horse Guards. Marshall Foch participated as representative of France. The weather was brilliant and the ground packed with sightseers.

Unfortunately the proposed naval and military parade could not take place, Hongkong, not being graced with the smiles which, according to Reuter, the sun bestowed on the historic trooping of the colours by the Horse Guards at Whitehall. However, lacking in that it was not found possible for it to take place." H.M. Navy and the mercantile boats in port "dressed ship."

The King's Birthday Ball followed a reception held by His Excellency the Governor (Sir Edward Stubbs, K.C.M.G.) at Government House yesterday evening, festivities commencing in the neighbourhood of 10 o'clock. The fairy "electric lamps" with which the paths in the garden were hung gave the grounds a most picturesque appearance and this could be best appreciated from the numerous sitting-out places on the lawns to which a covered and flag-bedecked way led from the House.

In the entrance hall was placed a large scarlet "Spider Hawkins" orchid and the staircase leading from there to the ball-room and the ball-room itself were pleasingly decorated with masses of pink hydrangeas whilst from the ceiling were suspended baskets of pink and white lotus. The verandahs and other rooms immediately adjoining the ball-room, on which supper was served, were also prettily decorated.

CONCERT CANCELLED
Owing to the late arrival of the Empress of Australia it will be impossible for Miss Mabal Garrison to give her concert this evening in the Theatre Royal as already advertised Mrs Garrison will give a recital to tomorrow evening. Tickets taken for this evening will be available tomorrow, or money will be returned upon application. Hongkong should not miss the opportunity of hearing one of the world's unique articles.
